typesense:trending.greeting:
*The post-summer chill hit Westchester hard this year, but it wasn't just the turn of the season making the Xavier Institute feel like a freezer.*

*A hate group’s anti-mutant strike had blown out half the mansion’s plumbing, taking out a chunk of the living room, the main kitchen, the central bathroom, and several bedrooms in a single violent flash. Rebuilding was an all-too-familiar routine, but Charles had approved an upgrade this time: a new wing featuring a small indoor pool, perfect for aquatic combat drills and surviving future heatwaves.*

*The problem? It was autumn. September rain lashed at the exposed framing, puddles pooled on the hardwood, warp lines rippled through the floorboards, and a stubborn scent of damp earth and black mold had begun to settle into the plaster.*

*Right now, the only spots with working heat were the underground basement, the Danger Room, Professor X’s office, and the cramped secondary living room. Kurt huddled near the basement heat vents, his blue fur damp from helping Scott patch the roof tarps. Upstairs, Hank and Ororo spent the afternoon setting up industrial dehumidifiers, though Ororo’s gentle attempts to warm the air currents only seemed to trigger localized condensation spikes.*

*"If we don't fix this airflow," Hank muttered, wiping frost from his glasses, "we’ll have a self-sustaining ecosystem growing in the west wing by Thanksgiving."*

*"We need heat, Scott," Rogue said, wrapped in three separate blankets in the tiny living room, shoulder-to-shoulder with Bobby, who was ironically complaining about the chill. "If we’re stuck crammed into three warm rooms until Christmas, somebody’s getting thrown through a wall."*

*Scott pinched the bridge of his nose, staring at the blueprints on the coffee table. "The contractors promise the drywalls go up next week. Until then... grab a shovel, clear the drainage, and draft the fire-emitters for heating duty."*
typesense:trending.name: X-Men
typesense:trending.title: cold winter
